To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the differential geometry of the space of paths (loops) of a manifold M, with respect to a principal G-bundle, is completely described by a pair (A,B), with A a connection on the bundle and B a closed 2-form on the base M.

we have found the differential geometry of the space of free loops and paths on a manifold M and we have found that the holonomy of the connection (A,B) on a surface is invariant under a suitable group action.

the space of free loops on a manifold M can be endowed with a principal G-bundle structure and that the holonomy of the connection is an invariant of the path of paths (or, equivalently, of the spanned surface) and that the holonomies of a connection A and of its curvature B are related by a non-abelian generalization of the Stokes formula.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the differential geometry and the quantum field theory aspects of four-dimensional BF-theories.
the geometry of the space of free loops and paths on M.
the differential geometry of the loop and path spaces, and with the construction of observables for the BF theories.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the space of paths is a natural setting to define and to study the observables for the BF theory.
the theory we are developing provides the right framework to study the quantum theory of BF theories in four dimensions.

the space of free loops on M is a good candidate as a phase space for a four-dimensional topological field theory, and in particular for a topological BF theory, in the sense of the work of Witten, Baez and others, and for a topological theory of quark confinement.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have been able to give a complete description of the geometry and of the observables of the quantum BF-theory.
we have developed a geometric language for the description of the observables of the BF theories, in the spirit of the Chern-Simons theories.
, by considering the space of loops as a base space for the bundle P, we are able to construct a non-abelian generalization of the classical Gauss-Bonnet-Chern theorem.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the holonomies of the theory are defined in terms of a non-abelian parallel transport along a path (or a surface) of paths (or surfaces).
, in order to obtain a consistent theory, the surface terms should depend only on the holonomy along the boundary of the surface, rather than on the holonomy of the whole surface.
the holonomy of a connection (A,B) is not only a function of the initial and the final point of the paths (loops) but depends on the whole spanned surface.
